origin: it should NOT report violation on consecutive aliases
source:
defmodule Test do
  alias App.Module1
  alias App.Module2
end

origin: it should NOT report violation on consecutive single-line multi-aliases
source:
defmodule Test do
  alias App.{Module1, Module2}
  alias App.Module2
end

origin: it should NOT report violation on consecutive multi-line multi-aliases
source:
defmodule Test do
  alias App

  alias App.{
    Module1,
    Module2
  }

  alias App.Module3
end

origin: it should NOT report violation on consecutive requires
source:
defmodule Test do
  require App.Module1
  require App.Module2
end

origin: it should NOT report violation on functions named require or alias
source:
defmodule Test do
  alias Foo
  require Foo

  defp require do
    :foo
  end

  defp alias do
    :foo
  end
end

origin: it should NOT report violation on multiline alias as
source:
defmodule Test do
  alias App.Module1

  alias App.Module2,
    as: Module3

  alias App.Module4
end

origin: it should NOT report violation on macro quotes
source:
defmodule Test do
  require Foo
  alias App.Module1

  defmacro __using__ do
    quote do
      alias App.Module2
    end
  end

  @doc false
  @impl true
  def run(%SourceFile{} = source_file, params \\ []) do
    issue_meta = IssueMeta.for(source_file, params)

    Credo.Code.prewalk(source_file, &traverse(&1, &2, issue_meta))
  end
end

origin: it should report violation on separate multi-line multi-aliases
source:
defmodule Test do
  alias App

  alias App.{
    Module1,
    Module2
  }

  require App.Module5

  alias App.Module3
end

findings.message: `alias` calls should be consecutive within a module.
